title: Dissent: Accountable Anonymous Group Messaging
note: Cost model: DC-net plus verifiable shuffle for moderate groups; later Dissent papers report this version usable only for 40-50 members. Trust: no honest-majority needed, accountability by blame protocol. Pre-2012, background.
bitmessage_link: Origin of the Dissent line; first anonymous group messaging with accountability against disruptors, which Bitmessage lacks (it relies on PoW only).

title: Dissent in Numbers: Making Strong Anonymity Scale
note: Cost model: client/server DC-net with anytrust servers. Scales to 5,000 online participants on DeterLab; latency as low as 600 ms for 600-client groups. Trust: anonymity holds if at least one of the M servers is honest. Round-based; every client talks every round.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Proactively Accountable Anonymous Messaging in Verdict
note: Cost model: verifiable DC-net with public-key proofs per message. Groups of 100 clients at 1 s per round, or 1,000 clients at 10 s per round. Trust: one honest server; no retroactive blame needed.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size. Adds proactive proofs against jamming, the DC-net analogue of Bitmessage's spam problem.

title: Security Analysis of Accountable Anonymity in Dissent
note: Cost model: no new performance numbers; hardened protocol with proofs of anonymity and accountability for moderate groups. Finds and fixes several attacks on the original Dissent protocol.
bitmessage_link: Formal proofs that hiding honest senders while exposing disruptors is possible; shows the kind of formal treatment Bitmessage never received.

title: Towards Provably-Secure Scalable Anonymous Broadcast
note: Cost model: targets the Omega(n^2) total bit complexity of classical DC-nets by using secure multiparty computation among small groups. Unconditional security against traffic analysis; theory with a protocol sketch, no deployment numbers.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Riposte: An Anonymous Messaging System Handling Millions of Users
note: Cost model: three servers, each client sends a DPF-compressed write per epoch (bandwidth about sqrt of board size). A three-server cluster built an anonymity set of 2,895,216 users in 32 hours (latency-tolerant). Trust: tolerates one malicious server (needs the other two to be non-colluding).
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size. Uses a bulletin board that every client writes to each epoch, like Bitmessage's shared object pool but with write-privacy and DoS audits.

title: Riffle: An Efficient Communication System With Strong Anonymity
note: Cost model: small set of servers plus many users; hybrid verifiable shuffle plus PIR. More than 100 KB/s per user in an anonymity set of 200 (file sharing); microblogging with over 100,000 users at under 10 s latency. Trust: one honest server.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size. Hybrid of verifiable shuffle for upload and PIR for download, the closest 2016 design to Bitmessage's two problems (upload source, download receiver).

title: PriFi: Low-Latency Anonymity for Organizational Networks
note: Cost model: client/relay/server DC-net; about 100 ms added latency for 100 clients, compatible with VoIP. Trust: remote servers assist anonymisation; defends equivocation attacks by history-dependent encryption.
bitmessage_link: DC-net variant for LANs that keeps client packets on their normal path; shows DC-nets can reach interactive latency when the anonymity set is local.

title: Untraceable VoIP Communication based on DC-nets
note: Cost model: DC-net adapted to streaming; two parties out of n communicate without disclosure, resilient to packet loss and faulty packets. No large-scale numbers; small-group scheme.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Express: Lowering the Cost of Metadata-hiding Communication with Cryptographic Privacy
note: Cost model: two servers, symmetric crypto only, one DPF write per message; over 100x less bandwidth than Pung and Riposte, end-to-end cost of a whistleblowing app 6x lower. Trust: secure against one malicious server and any number of malicious clients; no global round needed.
bitmessage_link: Mailbox model with write-privacy: senders write into a secret-shared mailbox table without servers learning which one, avoiding Bitmessage-style flooding; no synchronised rounds.

title: Spectrum: High-bandwidth Anonymous Broadcast
note: Cost model: two commodity servers; broadcasters share 1 GB in 13 h 20 min with an anonymity set of 10,000 (about USD 6.84 total); peak throughput 4 to 120,000 times faster than prior cryptographic systems in the broadcast setting. Trust: tolerates malicious clients and one malicious server (honest-but-non-colluding in the two-server setting).
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Clarion: Anonymous Communication from Multiparty Shuffling Protocols
note: Cost model: three-server broadcast secure against one malicious server using symmetric crypto; 9.2x faster than a mixnet of verifiable shuffles for 32-byte messages (3.0x for 160-byte) and 11.8x faster than the MCMix conversation protocol. Extension to k servers secure against k-1 malicious ones with costlier preprocessing.
bitmessage_link: Mixnet-style shuffling done jointly by servers on secret shares, so no per-server verifiable shuffle; a faster route to sender anonymity than Bitmessage's flooding.

title: Blinder: Scalable, Robust Anonymous Committed Broadcast
note: Cost model: MPC-based committed broadcast; evaluated with up to 1 million clients, up to 100 servers and 10 KB messages; a 5-server GPU implementation with 1 million clients has under 8 minutes latency, over 100x faster than 3-server Riposte. Trust: honest-majority servers (t < n/4), robust against malicious clients, global malicious network adversary, synchronous network.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Rabbit-Mix: Robust Algebraic Anonymous Broadcast from Additive Bases
note: Cost model: sender-anonymous broadcast with robustness and 100 percent delivery; about 3x fewer algebraic operations and less communication than Blinder, and removes Blinder's non-negligible failure probability. Trust: strong honest majority of servers.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Trellis: Robust and Scalable Metadata-private Anonymous Broadcast
note: Cost model: routing mixnet with anonymous routing tokens for verifiable random paths and lightweight blame protocols. With 64 servers over four regions, 220 bits per second with 100,000 users; 320 bits per second with 128 servers; 100 to 1000x slower than Tor. Trust: a fraction of servers may be malicious; guarantees availability for honest users.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Pepper: High-bandwidth and Scalable Anonymous Broadcast with Cryptographic Privacy
note: Cost model: DC-net with DPFs; millisecond-level registration audits, thousands of channels, 1.2 to 20x higher effective messaging rates than state-of-the-art alternatives (per abstract). Authorship list truncated to the first three names shown on the title page.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: A Survey on Anonymous Communication Systems with a Focus on Dining Cryptographers Networks
note: Cost model: survey, no new numbers. Useful for the DC-net family tree (Herbivore, Dissent, Verdict, Riposte, PriFi).
bitmessage_link: Survey of DC-net variants and what each trades for scalability and disruption resistance.

title: Towards Efficient Traffic-analysis Resistant Anonymity Networks
note: Cost model: high-bandwidth anonymity with constant-rate padded links; anonymity sets of hundreds of clients, latency low enough for bulk TCP; evaluated on traces of hundreds of thousands of BitTorrent users. Trust: tolerates a bounded number of compromised nodes.
bitmessage_link: Constant-rate, traffic-analysis-resistant forwarding for bulk traffic; shows what bandwidth cost buys source-timing resistance.

title: Herd: A Scalable, Traffic Analysis Resistant Anonymity Network for VoIP Systems
note: Cost model: dedicated cloud proxies fully interconnected plus untrusted superpeers; simulation on 370 million calls among 10.8 million users shows anonymity among millions at low bandwidth; superpeers cut trusted-infrastructure bandwidth and CPU by an order of magnitude; EC2 prototype delay suits high-quality calls. Trust: caller/callee anonymity within a trust zone.
bitmessage_link: Low-latency, traffic-analysis-resistant circuits for calls; anonymity among clients of one jurisdiction rather than a global flood.

title: Hydra: Practical Metadata Security for Contact Discovery, Messaging, and Dialing
note: Cost model: periodically (for example every ten minutes) built latency-aware, padded, onion-encrypted circuits used for connectionless contact requests and text; latency lower by an order of magnitude than round-based mixnet messengers; circuits upgradable to voice with slightly reduced anonymity. Trust: global observers, some malicious relays. Cited version is the SECRYPT 2021 paper.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Vuvuzela: Scalable Private Messaging Resistant to Traffic Analysis
note: Cost model: chain of servers, synchronous rounds; 68,000 messages per second for 1 million users at 37 s end-to-end latency on commodity servers; clients about 12 KB/s average (30 GB per month), servers about 166 MB/s with 1M users. Trust: privacy if at least one server is honest; differential privacy bounds leakage over time.
bitmessage_link: First system to give provable metadata privacy at million-user scale; replaces Bitmessage's broadcast with a server chain that adds differentially private noise and dead-drop exchange.

title: Alpenhorn: Bootstrapping Secure Communication without Leaking Metadata
note: Cost model: 10 million users on three servers with average dial latency 150 s and client bandwidth overhead 3.7 KB/s. Trust: anytrust (one honest server); IBE with threshold PKG servers.
bitmessage_link: Solves what Bitmessage leaves to chans and out-of-band exchange: private contact initiation with forward secrecy of metadata, using identity-based encryption and a keywheel.

title: Stadium: A Distributed Metadata-Private Messaging System
note: Cost model: parallel verifiable mixnet with distributed noise generation; supports 4x more users than Vuvuzela using servers that cost about an order of magnitude less; per-user bandwidth under 5x Vuvuzela; 100-server EC2 deployment. Trust: privacy against a fraction of malicious servers; differential privacy over routing links.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Karaoke: Distributed Private Messaging Immune to Passive Traffic Analysis
note: Cost model: latency 6.8 s for 2 million users with 100 servers, 5 to 10x better than Vuvuzela and Stadium; noise reduced by revealing leakage to clients only in the rare event (optimistic indistinguishability); Bloom filters check that noise is not discarded. Trust: differential privacy with a fraction of servers honest.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Atom: Horizontally Scaling Strong Anonymity
note: Cost model: 1,024 servers in anytrust groups carry a million Tweet-length messages in 28 minutes, over 23x faster than prior systems with similar guarantees; per-server bandwidth under 1 MB/s. Trust: anonymity among all honest users against an active network adversary and some servers, cryptographic not differential; latency of minutes, suited to short messages and dialing.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: XRD: Scalable Messaging System with Cryptographic Privacy
note: Cost model: 2 million users with 228 s latency using 100 servers, 13.3x faster than Atom and 4x faster than Pung; each user sends messages along many mix chains so the user upload grows with the square root of the number of servers. Trust: cryptographic privacy, no differential-privacy noise, honest users stay private if at least some chains are honest.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: MCMix: Anonymous Messaging via Secure Multiparty Computation
note: Cost model: dialing and conversation protocols implemented on Sharemind; scales to hundreds of thousands of users with latency competitive with weaker-guarantee systems. Trust: MPC threshold (honest majority of a small server set, Sharemind three-party).
bitmessage_link: MPC replaces mixnet or flooding: servers jointly compute the message exchange so no server learns who talks to whom.

title: The Loopix Anonymity System
note: Cost model: no synchronised rounds; a Loopix relay handles upwards of 300 messages per second with small delay; scales by adding mixes to a stratified topology; cost is extra bandwidth for cover traffic (clients send loops at Poisson rates). Trust: global passive adversary and active attacks; providers semi-trusted for storage, rate limiting; latency traded against anonymity by the delay parameter.
bitmessage_link: Message-oriented, asynchronous alternative to Bitmessage flooding: Poisson-delayed layered mixes with loop and drop cover traffic and semi-trusted providers that store mail for offline users.

title: Yodel: Strong Metadata Security for Voice Calls
note: Cost model: reusable circuits through a mix network using only symmetric crypto per message; 990 ms latency for 5 million simulated users with acceptable voice quality. Trust: global network adversary and compromised servers; guarded circuit exchange handles tampering.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: cMix: Mixing with Minimal Real-Time Asymmetric Cryptographic Operations
note: Cost model: fixed cascade; real-time phase only modular multiplications, no real-time public-key operations for users, scales linearly in users; basis of the xx network / Elixxir. Trust: strong anonymity if at least one cascade node is honest; precomputation is batch-based.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node. Moves public-key work to a precomputation phase so real-time mixing is a few modular multiplications.

title: Attacks on cMix - Some Small Overlooked Details
note: Cost model: none; analysis of overlooked details in the cMix protocol and fixes.
bitmessage_link: Active/insider attacks on cMix showing that the precomputation design needs extra checks.

title: Two Cents for Strong Anonymity: The Anonymous Post-office Protocol
note: Cost model: anonymous mailbox with sender anonymity via mixing and recipient anonymity via PIR-style retrieval; small payments used for DoS resistance; trade-offs stated in the paper rather than a single throughput figure.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which. Also like Bitmessage's PoW, it charges senders (micropayments) to resist spam.

title: AnNotify: A Private Notification Service
note: Cost model: scalable private notification service built on anonymous communication, sharding, dummy queries and Bloom filters; the paper computes the concrete advantage of an adversary observing multiple queries and evaluates costs; extensions for presence and broadcast notifications. A private publisher/subscriber event service, so it is core to the pub/sub corpus. Slug follows the other collector's copy (same file).
bitmessage_link: A private publish/subscribe-style notification service: a sender signals an event to a recipient without a broker learning who is notified, which is Bitmessage's broadcast problem in a lighter form.

title: HoneyBadgerMPC and AsynchroMix: Practical Asynchronous MPC and its Application to Anonymous Communication
note: Cost model: asynchronous MPC mixing robust to network delays; MPC-based mixnet with thousands of clients per batch. Trust: honest-majority threshold among servers, asynchrony tolerated.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: DumboMix: Robust Asynchronous Anonymous Broadcast Made Practical
note: Cost model: anonymous broadcast that keeps working under asynchrony; see paper for batch sizes. Trust: Byzantine fault tolerant server set.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: The Nym Network: The Next Generation of Privacy Infrastructure
note: Cost model: Loopix-style Poisson mixing with cover traffic; nodes rewarded via a proof-of-mixing / reputation scheme paid in NYM tokens; users hold anonymous credentials (Coconut) to prove right-to-use. Trust: global passive adversary; latency set by mix delay parameter. See the separate analysis papers for measured delays.
bitmessage_link: Loopix-derived, incentivised public mixnet with anonymous-credential access control; answers Bitmessage's free-rider and PoW admission model with paid, credentialed bandwidth.

title: Studying the anonymity trilemma with a discrete-event mix network simulator
note: Cost model: discrete-event simulator; evaluates how user load, topology and mixing strategy change anonymity and end-to-end latency in Elixxir, HOPR and Nym configurations. No fixed users-supported figure.
bitmessage_link: Quantifies anonymity, latency and bandwidth for Loopix-style, cMix-style (Elixxir) and HOPR designs; measurement-style evidence for the trilemma.

title: MiXiM: Mixnet Design Decisions and Empirical Evaluation
note: Cost model: framework to measure anonymity, end-to-end latency and traffic overhead for combinations of mixnet building blocks (topology, mixing strategy, cover traffic).
bitmessage_link: Simulation framework comparing threshold, timed, pool and Poisson mixing; informs how much delay buys against global observers.

title: Mixnet optimization methods
note: Cost model: methods to choose delays and topology to meet a target anonymity at minimal latency; shows variance in propagation delay and multi-core processing already helps when per-mix delay is very small.
bitmessage_link: Treats mixnet parameters as an optimisation problem; shows poor parameter choices give little or no protection.

title: Blending Different Latency Traffic With Beta Mixing
note: Cost model: mixes apply per-message delay parameters so users choose latency/anonymity per message; evaluated for anonymity gain of blending traffic classes.
bitmessage_link: Lets latency-tolerant and latency-sensitive traffic share one mixnet, so slow traffic (Bitmessage-like email) pads fast traffic.

title: Are continuous stop-and-go mixnets provably secure?
note: Cost model: no deployment numbers; derives conditions on delay distribution, cover traffic and honest-mix fraction under which continuous mixnets satisfy a formal anonymity definition (ePrint 2023/1311).
bitmessage_link: First end-to-end provable analysis of Loopix/Nym-style continuous-time mixing; the theoretical footing Bitmessage-style ad hoc designs lack.

title: No Right to Remain Silent: Isolating Malicious Mixes (Miranda)
note: Cost model: efficient alternative to proofs-of-shuffle; uses detection of faulty links and mixes with reduced connectivity; evaluated by simulation of how quickly corrupt mixes are isolated. Trust: malicious mixes up to a fraction.
bitmessage_link: Defence against active attacks (dropping, delaying) by mixes, the active-attack surface Bitmessage ignores.

title: Mixnets on a Tightrope: Quantifying the Leakage of Mix Networks Using a Provably Optimal Heuristic Adversary
note: Cost model: a lower-bound tool that samples observations; gives bounds on leakage for Karaoke and Atom topologies, with pitfalls for low-delay mixnets. Metadata only: IEEE copy not openly retrievable in this run.
bitmessage_link: Optimal adversary against recipient anonymity; shows low-delay topologies leak and gives bounds for the Karaoke and Atom routing designs.

title: LLMix: Quantifying Mix Network Privacy Erosion with Generative Models
note: Cost model: no system cost; shows a clear relation between number of captured messages and privacy loss, and that equal average-latency strategies are not equally unlinkable.
bitmessage_link: Learning-based adversary measuring how repeated observations erode mixnet anonymity over time (long-term intersection, which Bitmessage chans suffer too).

title: MixFlow: Assessing Mixnets Anonymity with Contrastive Architectures and Semantic Network Information
note: Cost model: attack; about 90 percent accuracy correlating chat flows even with cover traffic of 60 packets per minute and Poisson delay of 50 s.
bitmessage_link: Flow-correlation attack on Poisson-mixing designs: shows delay and cover alone do not stop end-to-end linking.

title: MixMatch: Flow Matching for Mixnet Traffic
note: Cost model: empirical attack on the Nym design with three classifiers (statistical and deep learning); real traffic datasets released. Tests Loopix-derived packet schedule with cover traffic against a passive observer.
bitmessage_link: Measures how well a passive adversary at the edges can match flows through Nym; cover traffic reduces but does not remove flow correlation.

title: LARMix: Latency-Aware Routing in Mix Networks
note: Cost model: propagation latency reduced as much as 8x (120 ms to 15 ms) with about 2 bits entropy loss; load balancing 3.5x latency cut while less than halving the anonymity set.
bitmessage_link: Cuts mixnet latency without a full anonymity penalty; shows the trilemma tuning that lets a low-latency mixnet replace Bitmessage's hours-long flooding.

title: LAMP: Lightweight Approaches for Latency Minimization in Mixnets with Practical Deployment Considerations
note: Cost model: 7.5x latency cut (153.4 ms to 20 ms) while keeping high anonymity; 3x better latency-anonymity trade-off than LARMix at about 13,900x lower compute.
bitmessage_link: Practical latency reduction evaluated on latency data from the deployed Nym mixnet.

title: LARMix++: Latency-Aware Routing in Mix Networks with Free Routes Topology
note: Cost model: latency-aware routing for free-route topologies; see LARMix for headline numbers.
bitmessage_link: Extension of LARMix to free-route (non-stratified) mixnets.

title: MALARIA: Management of Low-Latency Routing Impact on Mix Network Anonymity
note: Cost model: analysis of anonymity cost of latency-aware routing; no system numbers.
bitmessage_link: Quantifies how low-latency routing changes anonymity so that operators can choose a safe point.

title: MOCHA: Mixnet Optimization Considering Honest Client Anonymity
note: Cost model: routing optimisation; see paper for latency/anonymity numbers.
bitmessage_link: Optimises mixnet routing for the anonymity of honest clients.

title: OptiMix: Scalable and Distributed Approaches for Latency Optimization in Modern Mixnets
note: Cost model: distributed latency-optimisation approaches; see paper.
bitmessage_link: Distributed latency optimisation for modern mixnets.

title: Decentralized Reliability Estimation for Low-Latency Mixnets
note: Cost model: decentralised measurement using VRF-based sampling; no per-user bandwidth figure; targets mixnets whose nodes fail or drop packets (active-attack surface).
bitmessage_link: Lets mixnet clients estimate node reliability in a stateless per-packet-routed network (Nym).

title: Analysis and Attacks on the Reputation System of Nym
note: Cost model: none (attack analysis). Nym context stated in the paper: more than 550 nodes in 64 countries and about 3 billion packets per day; gateway plus up to three mix hops plus gateway; operators stake tokens and are selected into an active set by reputation. The paper attacks this reputation and selection system.
bitmessage_link: Attacks on the Nym reputation mechanism that decides which nodes carry traffic.

title: VeraSel: Verifiable Random Selection for Mixnets Construction
note: Cost model: verifiable randomness per epoch; compares overhead for building layers in large mixnets; no user-capacity numbers.
bitmessage_link: Verifiable random selection of mix nodes for stratified topologies, removing the need for a trusted directory.

title: Divide and Funnel: a Scaling Technique for Mix-Networks
note: Cost model: scaling technique distributing public-key work over many nodes without disconnecting message paths; sample anonymous broadcast protocol Streams carries 1 million messages with 16 s latency and 'one-in-a-billion' unlinkability, usable for anonymous microblogging and blockchain network-level anonymity.
bitmessage_link: Scaling technique that sets how many mixes users need for a target anonymity; follows from the anonymity-trilemma bounds.

title: sPAR: (Somewhat) Practical Anonymous Router
note: Cost model: practical construction of the Shi-Wu non-interactive anonymous router, where a single untrusted server permutes a set of messages without learning the permutation; aims to remove the need for any honest router and to fix the theory-only constructions. See paper for per-user costs. Trust: one untrusted server (cryptographic anonymity).
bitmessage_link: Anonymous router with cryptographic anonymity using lightweight primitives.

title: Verifiable SelfMix
note: Cost model: verifiable self-mix (VSM) for messages on a public bulletin board; users write their ciphertext to a hidden unique slot in a public table (Unique Number Selection plus Secure Mapping of Private Permutation), giving unconditional individual verifiability without trusting a mix server. Proofs in the malicious model; positioned between centralised mixnets and DC-net/MPC shuffles.
bitmessage_link: Verifiable mixing where users shuffle themselves.

title: Traceable mixnets
note: Cost model: mixnet variant that selectively reveals chosen input-output associations (tracing) while keeping the rest hidden; motivated by e-voting. No messaging cost numbers; relevant to accountability and abuse handling.
bitmessage_link: Tracing of mixed items for accountability, relevant to abuse handling in metadata-private systems.

title: OmniSphinx: Active Mix Networks
note: Cost model: see paper (mix network design resisting active adversaries).
bitmessage_link: Packet-format level defence against active attacks on Sphinx-like mixnets.

title: Hidden Services Protocol for Mixnets
note: Cost model: raising the Sphinx payload from 2 KiB to 10 KiB cuts mean page-load latency about 5.2x and payload overhead from 21.7 to 4.3 percent versus the current Nym baseline; deeper rewrap adds 0.3 to 0.6 s. Finds first/last-hop attacks on Nym SURB replies. Authorship list shows three names on the title page; further names may exist.
bitmessage_link: Receiver-anonymous services inside a mixnet; the mixnet analogue of Bitmessage's recipient privacy without flooding.

title: Are we collaborative yet? A Usability Perspective on Mixnet Latency for Real-Time Applications
note: Cost model: measures mixnet latency tolerance with users; compares with Tor latency.
bitmessage_link: User study on whether Nym-class latency suits real-time collaboration.

title: PANORAMIX Deliverable D4.4: Final System
note: Cost model: deliverable describes the integrated production system (peer authentication, PKI, audit logs, controller integration), not user capacity. Author list is the cover page (Galvez is editor).
bitmessage_link: Documents the EU project that produced Katzenpost: peer authentication, PKI, audit logs for Loopix-style mixnet operators.

title: Echomix: a Strong Anonymity System with Messaging
note: Cost model: Poisson-delayed mix layers, decoy loops, hybrid PQ nested packet encryption; the paper gives latency and bandwidth overhead evaluations. Trust: global adversary, compromised contacts and infrastructure, quantum adversaries; second-party (contact) adversary minimised.
bitmessage_link: Describes Katzenpost as a Loopix-descendant with PQ Sphinx, a group messaging protocol (BACAP and Pigeonhole) and store-and-retrieve for offline users; closest modern analogue of Bitmessage's object pool with metadata privacy.

title: Mixnet Research Review
note: Cost model: survey of designs; no new measurements.
bitmessage_link: Literature overview from a deployed-mixnet team: topology, compromising latency versus bandwidth, evolution since Chaum.

title: Post Quantum Sphinx
note: Cost model: two public-key operations per hop; X25519 pair costs about 160-233 ns on the author's laptop, KEM variants cost more and packet headers grow. KEM Sphinx is adopted by Katzenpost.
bitmessage_link: Post-quantum Sphinx variants (CSIDH-based NIKE and KEM Sphinx) for mixnets; fills the quantum gap in Bitmessage's static ECC keys.

title: Outfox: a Postquantum Packet Format for Layered Mixnets
note: Cost model: removes a full key exchange and uses compact per-hop headers, lowering computation and communication versus KEM-Sphinx. Applies to constant-length routes such as Loopix.
bitmessage_link: Sphinx-like format for fixed-length stratified routes with KEM-based per-hop keys and a UC security proof; the Nym packet format roadmap.

title: Provable Security for the Onion Routing and Mix Network Packet Format Sphinx
note: Cost model: no system numbers; adaptation embeds reply information in the payload and removes the nymserver at modest cost.
bitmessage_link: First detailed security proof of Sphinx; shows DDH is not enough (Gap-DH needed) and finds a sender-privacy attack on the integrated-system service model.

title: EROR: Efficient Repliable Onion Routing with Strong Provable Privacy
note: Cost model: efficient packet format with integrity protection; compared with other repliable onion schemes (heavier SNARG-based option).
bitmessage_link: Reply-capable onion packet format with hop-by-hop integrity, preventing tagging attacks that threaten both Sphinx and Bitmessage-like static-key designs.

title: Breaking and (Partially) Fixing Provably Secure Onion Routing
note: Cost model: none; proposes Tail-Indistinguishability and Layer-Unlinkability as repaired properties.
bitmessage_link: Shows the proof strategy behind HORNET and Sphinx-style formal security is flawed; links senders to receivers in HORNET data phase.

title: On Privacy Notions in Anonymous Communication
note: Cost model: none; proves a hierarchy among privacy notions.
bitmessage_link: Common vocabulary (sender, receiver, relationship anonymity, unobservability) to state what Bitmessage's flooding does and does not hide.

title: SoK on Performance Bounds in Anonymous Communication
note: Cost model: survey of lower bounds; no system numbers.
bitmessage_link: Systematises the proven latency, bandwidth and anonymity bounds that explain why Bitmessage's flood design is so expensive.

title: Anonymity Trilemma: Strong Anonymity, Low Bandwidth Overhead, Low Latency - Choose Two
note: Cost model: necessary relationships between bandwidth overhead, latency overhead and anonymity against a global passive adversary with a given number of compromised nodes; analyses many deployed designs.
bitmessage_link: Proves that strong anonymity needs either high bandwidth or high latency; Bitmessage picks high bandwidth (flood), Loopix picks latency.

title: Comprehensive Anonymity Trilemma: User Coordination is not enough
note: Cost model: bounds, no deployment numbers.
bitmessage_link: Extends the trilemma to protocols with user coordination (DC-net style); shows they cannot escape the bound alone.

title: SoK: Metadata-Protecting Communication Systems
note: Cost model: unified view of 31 systems against global network adversaries; compares trust assumptions, latency, scale. Use this as the cross-check for numbers quoted elsewhere in the catalog.
bitmessage_link: Best single comparison table of 31 systems (mixnets, DC-nets, PIR, TEE) with their cost and trust assumptions; the reference for this slice.

title: Unobservable Communication over Fully Untrusted Infrastructure (Pung)
note: Cost model: a 4-server deployment supports 135K messages per minute with 32K active users, 10^3 times more users than prior systems with the same threat model; clients incur 4.5 to 36 MB per message for multi-retrieval (k>1); latency of seconds. Trust: none (servers fully untrusted); computational PIR (XPIR) plus batch codes.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.

title: Talek: Private Group Messaging with Hidden Access Patterns
note: Cost model: a 3-server cluster reaches 9,433 messages per second for 32,000 active users at 1.7 s end-to-end latency; clients use about 148 MB per day; read interval trades bandwidth for latency. Trust: anytrust (one honest server), access-sequence indistinguishability.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which. Supports group channels (like Bitmessage chans) with hidden access patterns.

title: Addra: Metadata-private voice communication over fully untrusted infrastructure
note: Cost model: FastPIR; on 80 AWS machines serves 32K users with p99 message latency 726 ms, 7x better than Pung for text in the same threat model. Trust: none (fully untrusted infrastructure).
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.

title: Groove: Flexible Metadata-Private Messaging
note: Cost model: 100 AWS servers over four data centres give 32 s latency for 1 million users with 50 buddies; Pixel 4 client uses about 100 MB per month and adds 50 mW (16 percent battery). Trust: anytrust-style, one honest server.
bitmessage_link: Fixes the Bitmessage-relevant gaps of round-based systems: messages to offline buddies, multiple devices, low mobile cost, via oblivious delegation.

title: Distributed PIR: Scaling Private Messaging via the Users' Machines
note: Cost model: shifts most PIR computation to users' machines, 3.25x and 4.31x improvement over prior PIR-based messaging systems with the gap widening as users grow. Trust: no honest server required for privacy.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.

title: Pirates: Anonymous Group Calls over Fully Untrusted Infrastructure
note: Cost model: single server supports three-member group calls from 11 concurrent users with mouth-to-ear latency under 365 ms. Trust: none; unobservability even if all servers are malicious.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.

title: Myco: Unlocking Polylogarithmic Accesses in Metadata-Private Messaging
note: Cost model: oblivious data structure instead of PIR, so server work is O(N log^2 N) in the number of users N versus quadratic O(N^2) for PIR systems; throughput up to 302x better than multi-server and 2,219x better than single-server PIR-based systems. Trust: asymmetric two-server distributed trust (clients write to one server that obliviously forwards to a second server clients read from).
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.

title: Kerblam: Anonymous Messaging System Protecting Both Senders and Recipients
note: Cost model: two non-colluding servers; combines the HomeRun oblivious-message-retrieval protocol with an oblivious shuffle, then extends to larger messages with a two-server distributed scheme. Receivers need not stay online or trust an online proxy; no cap on messages sent or received. Trust: two non-colluding servers. See paper for throughput.
bitmessage_link: Combines sender mixing with oblivious message retrieval for the recipient, directly targeting Bitmessage's two privacy goals.

title: Formal Security Definition of Metadata-Private Messaging
note: Cost model: none; gives a complete definition of metadata-private messaging that accounts for compromised friends and describes a compromised-friend attack variant against Addra-style deployments (their Anysphere app). Slug follows the other collector's copy (same file).
bitmessage_link: Formal game for metadata-private messaging; basis for judging claims such as Bitmessage's.

title: Metadata-private Messaging without Coordination (PingPong)
note: Cost model: prototype with 32 8-core servers with enclaves; evaluated on a real messaging metadata dataset. Trust: trusted execution environments plus non-colluding servers (TEE trust).
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for sender and receiver to agree on a rendezvous address in advance, like Bitmessage's shared object pool but with enclave-protected retrieval.

title: PIR with Compressed Queries and Amortized Query Processing (SealPIR)
note: Cost model: queries up to 274x smaller than XPIR and 16.4x cheaper for the client, at 11 to 24 percent more server CPU; ported to Pung it cut network costs 36x and raised throughput 3x.
bitmessage_link: PIR building block that makes Pung-style mailboxes practical.

title: Spiral: Fast, High-Rate Single-Server PIR via FHE Composition
note: Cost model: at least 4.5x smaller queries, 1.5x smaller responses and 2x server throughput than previous systems; SpiralStreamPack 1.9 GB/s.
bitmessage_link: PIR building block for mailbox messaging.

title: OnionPIR: Response Efficient Single-Server PIR
note: Cost model: 4.2x response overhead versus 100x for SealPIR; a 30 KB entry needs 128 KB download.
bitmessage_link: PIR building block that cuts response size.

title: One Server for the Price of Two: Simple and Fast Single-Server Private Information Retrieval (SimplePIR/DoublePIR)
note: Cost model: SimplePIR about 10 GB/s/core server throughput, 121 MB hint per 1 GB database and 242 KB per query; DoublePIR shrinks hint to 16 MB, 345 KB per query, 7.4 GB/s/core.
bitmessage_link: High-throughput PIR with client hint; used as the PIR engine in recent messaging prototypes.

title: YPIR: High-Throughput Single-Server PIR with Silent Preprocessing
note: Cost model: 12.1 GB/s/core and 2.5 MB total communication for a 32 GB database with no offline communication.
bitmessage_link: PIR with no client-side hint, useful when messaging clients are stateless.

title: Oblivious Message Retrieval
note: Cost model: server cost about USD 1 per million messages scanned; digests decode in under 20 ms; board scan is linear per recipient. Trust: one non-colluding server cannot link recipients to messages.
bitmessage_link: Outsources trial-decryption: a server scans the whole board for a recipient and returns a compact digest without learning which messages are theirs, the direct cryptographic answer to Bitmessage's receiver download cost.

title: PerfOMR: Oblivious Message Retrieval with Reduced Communication and Computation
note: Cost model: see paper; reduces digest size and server cost versus the CRYPTO 2022 OMR.
bitmessage_link: OMR improvement with lower communication and computation.

title: HomeRun: High-efficiency Oblivious Message Retrieval, Unrestricted
note: Cost model: see paper.
bitmessage_link: OMR variant without a bound on pending messages.

title: Private Signaling
note: Cost model: server-aided private signaling; sender posts a message and a signal on a public board and only the recipient can tell it is theirs; constant work for sender and recipient (instead of scanning the board), full recipient privacy, UC-style definition. Compared against server-aided fuzzy message detection (Beck et al., CCS 2021), whose recipient work grows with privacy.
bitmessage_link: Server-assisted notification of a recipient without linking sender and recipient; includes a TEE-based instantiation.

title: Scalable Private Signaling
note: Cost model: see paper.
bitmessage_link: Improves private signaling scalability.

title: TEEMS: A Trusted Execution Environment based Metadata-protected Messaging System
note: Cost model: 220 clients in conversations in under 1 s with 205 cores, 18x better latency and throughput than prior work. Trust: TEE integrity and confidentiality (side channels excluded or mitigated by oblivious algorithms); distributed enclaves.
bitmessage_link: Enclave-based oblivious mailbox: servers hold messages in TEEs and route obliviously, so no flooding or trial decryption is needed.

title: ZIPNet: Low-bandwidth anonymous broadcast from (dis)Trusted Execution Environments
note: Cost model: DC-net-like anonymous vector scheme; 4.2x to 7.6x lower server runtime than the state of the art; outsources almost all server inbound traffic and about 80 percent of computation to aggregators that are untrusted for anonymity; scales to hundreds of any-trust servers (trust diversity). Trust: anytrust servers (as Dissent) for privacy; client-side TEEs used only for DoS prevention, not for privacy, so a broken TEE does not de-anonymise.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Enhancing Security and Privacy of Tor's Ecosystem by using Trusted Execution Environments (SGX-Tor)
note: Cost model: end-to-end latency overhead 3.9 percent and throughput overhead 11.9 percent for HTTP. Trust: SGX attestation; excludes side channels.
bitmessage_link: Trusted-hardware relays reduce a malicious relay to a network-level adversary; the TEE analogue of attesting Bitmessage nodes.

title: Mobile Private Contact Discovery at Scale
note: Cost model: online phase 2.92 s on WiFi (6.53 s on LTE) to check 1,024 contacts against a database of 2^28 entries. Trust: PSI without hardware; malicious clients handled.
bitmessage_link: Private contact discovery by PSI, integrated into the Signal client; the non-TEE alternative to Signal's SGX contact discovery.

title: All the Numbers are US: Large-scale Abuse of Contact Discovery in Mobile Messengers
note: Cost model: crawling cost to enumerate large parts of WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram membership; proposes mitigations. Trust: service operator and TEE-based discovery reviewed.
bitmessage_link: Shows that even deployed contact discovery leaks the whole user directory by crawling, a lesson for any scheme that publishes recipient identifiers (Bitmessage addresses are likewise enumerable).

title: Scaling Mobile Private Contact Discovery to Billions of Users
note: Cost model: see paper; targets WhatsApp-scale user bases.
bitmessage_link: Contact discovery for billions of users using PSI/PIR hybrids.

title: Zephyr: Hiding Metadata in a Messaging System
note: Cost model: small mixnet messaging proposal (high-school preprint); no scale numbers. Included for completeness only.
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Strong Anonymity for Mesh Messaging
note: Cost model: 200 users each sending every 30 s under pessimistic crowd density; more than 3,000 users each sending every minute under more realistic assumptions. Trust: no central server; global passive observers of the mesh.
bitmessage_link: Anonymous messaging over phone-to-phone mesh networks without Internet, the setting where flooding (Bitmessage-style) is natural; shows how to add strong anonymity.

title: Private Identity-based Bulletin Boards for Anonymous Messaging and Other Online Services
note: Cost model: HIBE with searchable ciphertexts; posts to non-colluding servers and receiver retrieval later; see paper for latency and throughput. Trust: non-colluding servers.
bitmessage_link: Lets a sender post to a receiver known only by an identity (email address, pseudonym) without prior key exchange; Bitmessage addresses are such identities.

title: Remise: Authorized Anonymous Communication Systems
note: Cost model: two-server authorised anonymous communication on Distributed ORAM, in two modes (public anonymous bulletin board per epoch, and secret-shared channels with grantable and revocable read access); 80x lower online server time than PACL (Spectrum) for databases of size 2^24. Trust: at least one of two servers honest.
bitmessage_link: Adds authorised-sender access control to DPF-based anonymous mailboxes; analogue of Bitmessage's PoW admission control but with credentials.

title: Sabre: Sender-Anonymous Messaging with Fast Audits
note: Cost model: Riposte/Express-style structure with logarithmic-cost audit protocols instead of linear; order of magnitude better under ideal conditions and asymptotic speed-up under resource-exhaustion DoS. Trust: two or three non-colluding servers. Metadata only: no open PDF located in this run.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: Onion Franking: Abuse Reports for Mix-Based Private Messaging
note: Cost model: abuse-reporting mechanisms for any onion-encrypted private messaging system, including low-latency opportunistic mixing and mixnets; claims lower overhead than prior metadata-hiding abuse reporting and stronger threat models; see paper for numbers.
bitmessage_link: Abuse reporting for mix-based systems; handles the spam/abuse problem that Bitmessage handled only with proof-of-work.

title: Abuse Reporting for Metadata-Hiding Communication Based on Secret Sharing
note: Cost model: see paper.
bitmessage_link: Abuse reports in secret-sharing-based systems such as Express and Riposte.

title: Asymmetric Message Franking: Content Moderation for Metadata-Private End-to-End Encryption
note: Cost model: see paper.
bitmessage_link: Abuse reporting compatible with metadata hiding; counterpart to Bitmessage's absence of any reporting.

title: Ruffle: Rapid 3-party shuffle protocols
note: Cost model: see paper.
bitmessage_link: Fast 3-party shuffle usable for mixing in MPC-based anonymous messaging.

title: Footprint scheduling for Dining-Cryptographer networks
note: Cost model: replaces slot-reservation rounds with footprint scheduling to lower overhead; no deployment numbers.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size. Solves the slot reservation step of DC-nets.

title: HOPR - a Decentralized and Metadata-Private Messaging Protocol with Incentives
note: Cost model: probabilistic micropayments and proof of relay pay each relay; cost scales with relay hops and cover traffic; the whitepaper has no user-capacity measurements (Piotrowska's simulator paper evaluates HOPR). Trust: no trusted relays; blockchain settlement. Date from the cover page; later revisions exist.
bitmessage_link: Incentivised decentralised relay network with payment-channel proof-of-relay; the economic answer to Bitmessage's PoW-only admission, with metadata privacy from relayed packets rather than flooding.

title: Katzenpost Mix Network Specification
note: Cost model: high-level architecture of a Loopix-style decryption mixnet with entry, middle and service layers, directory authorities, Poisson mix delays and loop decoys; no throughput figures. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

title: Katzenpost Sphinx Cryptographic Packet Format Specification
note: Cost model: fixed-size packets, per-hop DH blinding, SURB replies. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Concrete Sphinx parameterisation used by Katzenpost; the packet format layer that stops per-hop linking.

title: KEM Sphinx Packet Format (Katzenpost specification)
note: Cost model: replaces NIKE with KEM at the price of larger headers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: KEM-based Sphinx preserving bitwise unlinkability, constant packet size and route-length hiding.

title: Pigeonhole Protocol Specification (Katzenpost)
note: Cost model: box-based streams (BACAP), all-or-nothing group writes; no throughput numbers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Replaces mailbox servers with scattered storage: clients write and read pseudorandom boxes through the mixnet, a direct successor to Bitmessage's shared object store.

title: Group Chat Specification (Katzenpost)
note: Cost model: depends on Pigeonhole; no numbers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Group messaging on Pigeonhole boxes, the mixnet counterpart of Bitmessage chans.

title: Sphinx Packet Replay Detection (Katzenpost specification)
note: Cost model: memory per node grows with packets per epoch. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Replay detection that Bitmessage handles with object-hash dedup; here per-hop tag caches with epoch rotation.

title: Propagation of mix decoy loop statistics (Katzenpost specification)
note: Cost model: extra statistics traffic with directory authority. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
bitmessage_link: Defence against (n-1) attacks that use strategic packet loss: nodes publish decoy-loop statistics.

title: Sphinx: A Compact and Provably Secure Mix Format
note: Cost model: constant-size packets, one group element per hop plus MAC. Background reference.
bitmessage_link: Packet format used by Loopix, Nym, Katzenpost and the Lightning Network; contrast with Bitmessage's single-layer static-key encryption.

title: Herbivore: A Scalable and Efficient Protocol for Anonymous Communication
note: Cost model: DC-net cliques of small size; later Dissent papers report Herbivore-class systems usable only up to 40-50 participants. Background.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.

title: TARANET: Traffic-Analysis Resistant Anonymity at the NETwork layer
note: Cost model: prototype forwards anonymous traffic at over 50 Gbps on commodity hardware; mixing in setup phase, constant-rate shaping in data phase. Trust: end hosts and ASes coordinate; some compromised ASes tolerated.
bitmessage_link: Network-layer traffic-analysis resistance: mixing during setup, then constant-rate transmission via packet splitting; contrasts with Bitmessage's application-layer flooding.

title: Strong and Scalable Metadata Security for Voice Calls
note: Cost model: see the constituent papers (Alpenhorn, Karaoke, Yodel) in this catalog.
bitmessage_link: Collects Alpenhorn, Karaoke and Yodel in one design narrative from the author who built the Vuvuzela family.

title: Verbeth: Secure Messaging with Metadata Minimization over Public Blockchain Logs
note: Cost model: no server of its own; economics and size limits of on-chain messaging analysed; first-contact discovery either long-term-key KEM with trial decryption (cost grows with the log) or private signaling backed by trusted hardware; topic rotation driven by the double-ratchet state. Main contribution is an analysis of metadata leakage under several adversaries.
bitmessage_link: Closest modern relative of Bitmessage: public log as the transport, first contact by KEM with trial decryption (or a TEE-backed private signaling service), then per-conversation topic rotation so conversations are unlinkable.

title: Mitigating Intersection Attacks in Anonymous Microblogging
note: Cost model: protocol groups users into anonymity sets by publishing behaviour and gives each set a configurable communication schedule that trades latency against bandwidth; evaluated by simulating Twitter and Reddit publishing data; anonymity set degrades slowly under churn.
bitmessage_link: Long-term intersection attacks on anonymous broadcast, which hit Bitmessage chans and any system with churn.

title: Technology preview: Private contact discovery for Signal
note: Cost model: contact lookups run inside a server-side SGX enclave with remote attestation; the post explains that host-visible memory access patterns and the 128 MB encrypted memory limit defeat a naive hash-table lookup, that general ORAM (Path ORAM, recursive) fits poorly for huge key sets with empty values, and that a deliberately oblivious linear scan is the workable design. Trust: hardware vendor and enclave integrity; side channels acknowledged. Page saved as Markdown; technical blog post by a Signal author, accepted because it is the design description of a deployed service.
bitmessage_link: Engineering description of hiding who looks up whom from a service operator with an SGX enclave; the enclave lessons (memory access patterns, small encrypted memory, ORAM not fitting) apply to any receiver-private lookup.
